description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-31 while running the mandated Android proxy check for op-9vo6.2.

SYMPTOM: cargo check -p kovan --lib --target aarch64-linux-android failed with 12 errors in rfd v0.17.2 ('error: could not compile rfd'). This is a violation of CLAUDE.md's Android/Termux HARD RULE, which puts kovan's library plus its kovan-cli and kovan-tui binaries explicitly IN scope (only the kovan GUI binary is exempt, behind the gui feature).

CAUSE: crates/kovan/Cargo.toml:107 declared

    kopitiam-pdf = "0.3.1"

unconditionally -- NOT inside the [target.'cfg(not(target_os = "android"))'.dependencies] block at line 180. kopitiam-pdf 0.3.1's feature table is default = ["kpdf"], kpdf = ["dep:eframe", "dep:egui", "dep:rfd"], so taking it with default features dragged eframe/egui/rfd into the LIBRARY's unconditional dependency graph. cargo tree -p kovan --target aarch64-linux-android -i rfd confirmed the single path: rfd v0.17.2 <- kopitiam-pdf v0.3.1 <- kovan.

FIX (one line):

    kopitiam-pdf = { version = "0.3.1", default-features = false }

kovan only uses kopitiam_pdf::mupdf::{PdfDocument, rasterize_page, page_to_stext, interpret::Processor}, which is core to the crate and NOT behind the kpdf feature -- kpdf only adds the standalone-shell dependencies. Nothing is lost: kovan's own GUI file picker is egui_file_dialog::FileDialog (its own egui-file-dialog dependency), never kopitiam's rfd.

VERIFIED:
  cargo check -p kovan --lib         --target aarch64-linux-android  -- clean
  cargo check -p kovan --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android  -- clean (lib + kovan-cli + kovan-tui; the kovan GUI bin is correctly excluded by its gui feature gate)
  cargo check -p kovan --all-targets                                  -- clean (desktop, gui feature on by default; eframe/egui-file-dialog still compile)
  cargo test  --release -p kovan --lib --tests                        -- 230 + 15 + 17 + 7 passing
  cargo check --workspace --lib --tests                               -- clean

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this -- a --lib-only Android check misses broken examples/tests/benches, and evidently nobody had run even the --lib check since kopitiam-pdf became a kovan dependency. Note commit 5e504e3f ('moved kovan to use v0.3.1 of kopitiam pdf') is when the current pin landed, but the unconditional declaration predates it.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH CONSIDERING: when kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2 lands (op-9zef, kopitiam#96), its reusable pieces move behind a separate egui feature distinct from the kpdf standalone shell. Re-check this declaration then -- the desktop GUI may want the egui feature explicitly, and it must stay off for Android.
title: kovan: library did not build for Android -- kopitiam-pdf's default kpdf feature pulled rfd

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


A bridge **must not create or destroy matter**.

Enforce: total mass; C; H; O; N; S; and additional elements where represented
(Cl once PVC chemistry exists, metals, catalyst inventories).

Where both packages share a species basis, **species inventory is preserved
exactly**. Where representation also changes, defer to the representation
bridge, which carries its own conservation obligations.

**Conservation failure must be loud. Do not silently normalize a materially
inconsistent stream** — a normalized stream is a wrong answer that looks
right, and it will propagate through every downstream unit.

Elemental inventory is checkable independently of any package, which is exactly
why it is the right invariant to enforce here.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Elemental conservation framework

description:
Raised by the implementing agent 2026-08-11 as part of op-jyyp.1 (landed in commit 4feb6c84, crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../solid_database/nuclear_graphite.rs, 871 lines, 6 V&V tests). Both assumptions are documented at the site rather than hidden, but both should be reviewed before any result depending on them is trusted.

1. ONE cp CURVE SERVES BOTH GRADES. The specific-heat table is grade-insensitive: NuclearGraphiteMatrixA3 and NuclearGraphiteIG110 dispatch to the same shared enthalpy and cp functions. The enum arms were deliberately duplicated per variant rather than collapsed into an or-pattern, precisely so this decision stays greppable and has to be revisited explicitly if the assumption is challenged. Check whether the grades genuinely share a cp curve within the accuracy this work needs.

2. THE A3 DAMAGE FACTOR IS APPLIED TO IG-110, WHICH THE VTB DOES NOT DO. The fast-neutron-fluence conductivity degradation was fitted for matrix graphite A3 and is being reused for IG-110. The source the correlations came from does not make that extension. Irradiated reflector conductivity drives the passive decay-heat path, so if IG-110 degrades differently this propagates straight into the loss-of-forced-cooling result — the exact place where an optimistic error makes the safety case look better than it is.

WHAT THE TESTS ACTUALLY ESTABLISH, per the implementing agent: "Nothing here is checked against HTR-10 measurements. The tests verify transcription and interpolation against hand evaluations of the same formulas — that is all they establish." The word "validated" appears nowhere in the added code or docs, correctly.

Measured behaviour for reference: damage factor is 1.0 at zero fluence and 0.139 at gam = 15, still positive, with the zero crossing near gam = 19. The fluence gate is [0, 15] and returns an error rather than clamping.
title: TUAS nuclear graphite: two documented assumptions carrying real physical risk

description:
Found 2026-08-12 while implementing crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs (op-62vf).

DEFECT. interfaces/functional_programming/pt_flash_eqm/mod.rs:134 classifies a (T,p) point as the two-phase Region 4 with an EXACT float equality:

    (temp, pres) if (273.15..647.096).contains(&temp) && pres == p_sat_reg4_pascal => FwdEqnRegion::Region4

and every Region-4 arm of that module then panic!s (cp at :211, h at :171, s at :198, v at :242, w at :256, ...), because (T,p) cannot resolve a saturated mixture without a quality.

CONSEQUENCE. tampines::multiphase_1d::properties::SaturatedTransport::at(p) evaluates lambda_tp_eqm_two_phase at exactly (T_sat(p), p); the critical-enhancement term calls cp_tp_eqm_single_phase; so SaturatedTransport::at PANICS for every pressure p that round-trips bit-exactly through sat_pressure_4(sat_temp_4(p)).

MEASURED (2026-08-12, release), geometric sweep of 10790 pressures from 1.0e5 Pa to 2.2e7 Pa at ratio 1.0005:
  - SaturatedTransport::at panics: 105 (about 1 percent), scattered rather than banded
  - predicted by the bit-exact round-trip: 105, with ZERO false positives and ZERO false negatives
  - SaturatedProperties::at panics: 0 (it never routes through the classifier)

A blowdown sweeps continuously through pressure, so hitting one is a certainty, and it aborts the whole march with a panic rather than a Result.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS:
1. A panic where an error belongs. interfaces/checked exists; the functional path should return Result rather than panic, or SaturatedTransport should use a quality-explicit entry point.
2. An exact float comparison on a region boundary. Even setting the panic aside, 'pres == p_sat_reg4_pascal' is not a defensible region test.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE (consumer side, not a fix): tampines::multiphase_1d::two_fluid::region_4_safe_pressure nudges p by a relative 4e-12 when and only when the bit-exact round-trip fires. Pinned by two_fluid_tests::region_4_safe_pressure_removes_the_upstream_classifier_panic, which re-measures the sweep and asserts zero mispredictions and zero surviving panics. Remove the workaround only after fixing the library and re-running that test.
title: tampines-steam-tables: pt_flash_eqm region classifier panics on exact float equality at the Region-4 line

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


**A normal supported case, not an edge case:**

```
hot side:  petroleum pseudocomponents + PR
cold side: water/steam + IAPWS
```

The solver uses **each side's own thermo package** and enforces
`Q_hot + Q_cold + losses = 0` within tolerance.

**Do not attempt to construct one shared property package for both sides.**
Forcing steam into a petroleum cubic EOS to match the process side is exactly
the wrong answer, and gives up the IAPWS accuracy the steam tables exist to
provide.

This is the first place the epic pays off visibly, and a good early acceptance
test: it needs no reactive chemistry, both packages already exist, and energy
closure is directly checkable.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Multi-package heat exchanger

description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 on ENDF/B-VIII.0 U-238 (reference-data/endf/n-092_U_238.endf), found while chasing op-mzvp.2.12.

THE DEFECT. broadr::doppler_broaden(sections, awr, temp_k) has no upper energy bound: it broadens every point of every section. Upstream NJOY bounds BROADR with thnmax (max energy for broadening) and never runs SIGMA1 above the resolved range, because there the evaluation holds energy-AVERAGED values, not the pointwise sigma(E) the SIGMA1 kernel assumes. 'thnmax' appears nowhere in this crate.

EVIDENCE. U-238's resolved range ends at 20 keV; MF=3/MT=102 is discontinuous there (0.0 b below, 0.52987 b above -- both tabulated at E=2.0e4). Stage-isolated with examples/seam_stage_probe.rs (--features urr-diagnostics):

  AFTER RECONR (0 K):   E=2.0e4 sigma=0.56018 b  (resolved side)
                        E=2.0e4 sigma=0.52987 b  (unresolved side, MF=3)
  AFTER BROADR (600 K): E=2.0e4 sigma=0.29114 b
                        E=2.0e4 sigma=0.29114 b

RECONR carries the ENDF discontinuity correctly. BROADR collapses both sides onto one wrong value by smearing resolved resonance structure across the boundary. Because the evaluation's next MF=3 point is 24 keV, the error is then linearly interpolated over the whole 20-24 keV segment: 45% low at the seam, still ~37% low at 20.5 keV, converged by 24 keV.

SCOPE. Sign is right to inflate k (less capture -> higher resonance escape), but 20-24 keV is only 0.18 lethargy units, so this is worth tens to low hundreds of pcm -- NOT the +2854 pcm of op-mzvp.2.12. Affects every evaluation with a resolved/unresolved boundary, not just U-238.

THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. Two attempts failed and are recorded so they are not repeated: (1) preserving the duplicate point in reconr::rebuild_range works at the RECONR stage but BROADR flattens it anyway; (2) adding a doppler_broaden_below(.., e_upper) bound has no effect on the seam, because BOTH duplicate points sit exactly AT eh and 'e > e_upper' excludes neither. A correct fix needs BROADR to be discontinuity-aware at its boundary -- the SIGMA1 grid is index-based and a duplicated energy is degenerate in it. Needs its own V&V.

Related: op-mzvp.2.12 (the ring-RPT case this was found under), op-cjw.6 (UNRESR/PURR verification -- the architecturally correct home for URR temperature dependence and self-shielding, which must NOT come from SIGMA1).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
LEAD from the 2026-09-10 ring-RPT baseline run (op-mzvp.2.12 reproduced exactly): the unbounded BROADR may also be smearing REACTION THRESHOLDS, not just the URR seam.

Six-factor, our ring-RPT CSG pebble vs OpenMC ring-RPT:
  eta 2.0158 vs 2.0073   (+0.42%)
  f   0.9140 vs 0.9216   (-0.82%)
  p   0.5279 vs 0.4842   (+9.03%)
  eps 1.4109 vs 1.5043   (-6.21%)
  k   1.39333 +/- 0.00219 vs 1.36479 +/- 0.00067  = +2854 pcm

p too high is too little resonance absorption -- the right direction for this bead's 20-24 keV capture deficit, though far too narrow a band to explain 9%.

But eps too LOW by 6.2% is fast-fission physics at MeV energies, which no URR treatment touches. HYPOTHESIS: doppler_broaden has no upper bound at all, so SIGMA1 runs over the entire grid to 20 MeV, including across MF=3 reaction THRESHOLDS (U-238 MT=18 fission onset ~0.6-1 MeV, MT=16 n2n onset). A threshold is a discontinuity in the same sense the 20 keV seam is; smearing it would depress sigma_f just above onset, which lowers eps -- the observed sign.

TO CHECK (cheap, same method as seam_stage_probe): dump U-238 MT=18 around its threshold after RECONR and after BROADR and compare against the tape's own MF=3/MT=18. If BROADR is rounding the onset, that is the same defect as this bead with a second, larger consequence, and thnmax fixes both.

If confirmed this materially raises the value of fixing op-sdbk: currently scoped at tens to low hundreds of pcm from the URR seam alone.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-09-10 (this session), upstream read first per the new CLAUDE.md rule. What upstream actually does -- three mechanisms, none of them 'discontinuity-aware SIGMA1':

(1) reconr.f90 rdfil2 'shade nodes to prevent discontinuities' (l.745-777) and lunion 'check ahead for discontinuity': a PENDF NEVER holds two points at one energy. A tabulated step at E is written as sigfig(E,7,-1) / sigfig(E,7,+1) (2e4 -> 1.999999e4 / 2.000001e4), and the resonance-range boundary nodes EL/EH are placed at the same shaded energies. If the two sigma values are equal the duplicate is dropped.
(2) broadr.f90 thnmax (l.107-124 doc, l.354-441 code): default thnmax = EH of the first MF=2 range record as RECONR rewrote it (= eresr, top of the resolved range; = start of the URR if no resolved range; LRU=0 range top for non-resonance nuclides), capped at 6.5 MeV (e6pt5), never above MF=1 EMAX, and for LRP=0 lowered to 0.99999*first threshold. Points with E > thnmax are copied through verbatim (label 190, l.1493-1503); the node AT thnmax is still broadened; bsigma integrates over all three loaded pages, so the last resolved-side point does see the step above it. (3) broadr.f90:483 fact=0.99999 nudges the lower of any residual duplicate pair down on the union grid.

Also checked stounx/getunx (MT152 subtraction before broadening, re-add after): for U-238 eumax==e1 so nunr=0 -> 'no overlap, unresolved not needed' -> it does NOTHING here. Not the mechanism.

WHY THE TWO EARLIER ATTEMPTS FAILED: both left the seam as two points at exactly 2e4. With (1) the seam is two DISTINCT energies straddling thnmax, so a plain 'E <= thnmax broaden / E > thnmax copy' rule is sufficient -- that is the entire upstream trick.

BASELINE ON PRISTINE DEVELOP e09239ee (seam_stage_probe, MT=102, 600 K): RECONR emitted ONE point at 2.0e4 = 0.56018 b (rebuild_range dedup collapsed the pair: URR value 0.52987 + resonance tail 0.0302 -- so the discontinuity was already lost at RECONR, and 6% high at 0 K), BROADR gave 0.30629 b there; 46.7% low at the seam, 41% low at 20.5 keV, 25% low at 22 keV (interpolated to the 24 keV point).

FIX (commit on develop): reconr::shade_discontinuities (lunion) + shaded EL/EH nodes in rebuild_range (rdfil2); ResonanceInfo::pendf_resonance_upper_limit + ReconrResult.resonance_upper_limit (eresr/eresh); broadr::broadening_limit (thnmax rules i/ii/iii + emax cap + e6pt5 fallback), broadr::doppler_broaden_below, broadr::broaden_result; interface.rs, outram-mc-libs Nuclide::from_tape and the examples switched to the bounded path. doppler_broaden (unbounded) kept as the bare kernel.

MEASURED AFTER FIX (same probe): RECONR 1.999999e4 = 0.03021 b (resolved side, MF3=0 + tail), 2.000001e4 = 0.529870 b (exact tape). Bounded BROADR 600 K: 2.000001e4 = 0.529870 (bit-identical), 20.5/21/22/23 keV = 0.52262/0.51536/0.50086/0.48635 = tape lin-lin exactly; resolved-side point 1.999999e4 broadened to 0.2810 b (sees the step, as upstream's does). Regression test tests/broadr_u238_urr_seam.rs also asserts every point above thnmax of MT1/2/18/102 is copied bit-for-bit.

NEGATIVE RESULT on the fast-fission lead (comment above): prediction before measuring -- Doppler width at 1 MeV for U-238/600 K is sqrt(4 E kT/A) ~ 30 eV, SIGMA1 is integral-preserving, so a threshold can only move over tens of eV with no net depression. Measured with the UNBOUNDED (pre-fix) kernel: MT=18 over 0.8-2.0 MeV deviates from the tape by <= 0.04% (worst +0.039% at 1.0 MeV); MT=16 (n,2n) onset 6.179 MeV: 1.0e-6 b at the onset point, +0.07% at 6.3 MeV, +0.01% at 6.5 MeV. Note U-238 MT=18 has no hard threshold at all (sub-threshold fission tabulated from 1e-5 eV). BROADR was NOT depressing eps; the 6.2% low fast-fission factor is not a BROADR effect and needs a different lead. With thnmax=2e4 the bounded kernel now leaves everything above 20 keV untouched anyway (0.000% at every point checked).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: ORACLE CONFIRMATION 2026-09-10: NJOY2016 itself (commit ac5adf5, built in-session with gfortran 13.3.0 at upstream_source/NJOY2016/build/njoy, gitignored) run on the same U-238 tape with reconr 0.001 + broadr 600 K. Its listing: 'resolved resonance range upper limit = 2.00000E+04 eV', 'final maximum energy for broadening/thinning = 2.00000E+04 eV'. Its PENDF MF3/MT102: 1.9999990e4 -> 0.2809805 b, 2.0000010e4 -> 0.5298699 b, and lin-lin at 20.5/21/22/23 keV = 0.52262/0.51536/0.50086/0.48635 b. The fixed port: 0.2809594 (7e-5 rel) and 0.529870 at the two shaded points, and 0.52262/0.51536/0.50086/0.48635 -- identical to every printed digit. Pre-fix port at 20.5 keV was 0.30593. These oracle values are now asserted in tests/broadr_u238_urr_seam.rs. Also confirmed on U-235: NJOY prints 'final maximum energy for broadening/thinning = 2.25000E+03 eV' (top of its resolved range), as broadening_limit() computes.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Fixed on develop (31fa3880 + follow-up): RECONR shades discontinuities and range-boundary nodes as upstream lunion/rdfil2 do (sigfig +-1), BROADR gained thnmax (broadening_limit / doppler_broaden_below / broaden_result; interface.rs and outram-mc-libs use it). Verified against NJOY2016 itself on the same U-238 tape at 600 K: seam values and 20.5-23 keV interpolants identical to every printed digit. Fast-fission threshold hypothesis measured and rejected (unbounded kernel moves MT=18 by <=0.04% over 0.8-2 MeV, MT=16 by <=0.07%). Regression: tests/broadr_u238_urr_seam.rs.

title: njoy BROADR has no thnmax: SIGMA1 runs across the resolved/unresolved seam and destroys the URR anchor
